page: Amazon Web Services r7i.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by custom 4th Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (model 8488C). The instance features 16 virtual CPUs derived from 8 dedicated physical cores with multithreading active, operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz. Its x86_64 architecture incorporates 105 MB of L3 cache alongside specialized instruction extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which accelerate targeted vectorized and matrix arithmetic operations.

Memory capacity is configured at 128 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance carries no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent filesystem needs, and provides a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps without discrete GPU hardware acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate solid single-thread performance, highlighted by top-quartile results in Geekbench single-core tests (2141.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (33.78 GB/sec), while small-model LLM text generation reaches the top ten percent (333.12 tokens/sec). Broader multi-core computational metrics, memory bandwidth under large uncached blocks, and PassMark database operations consistently measure within the median 50 percent.

From an efficiency standpoint, the r7i.4xlarge optimizes resource density for workloads demanding high memory capacity per thread without paying for unused GPU silicon or dedicated local NVMe drives. Primary operational fits include in-memory databases such as Redis or Memcached, intermediate relational database servers, distributed memory caches, enterprise data processing, and single-node in-memory analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r7i.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the Nitro System, featuring a 16-vCPU, 8-physical-core Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 128 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, the instance delivers an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive operations. It includes modern vector and matrix instructions via AVX-512 and Intel AMX, but lacks integrated local storage and GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached volumes alongside a 6 Gbps network baseline. Synthetic testing displays strong single-threaded execution and lightweight model inference, while overall multi-core throughput and memory access latency align with mid-range industry baselines. The r7i.4xlarge provides balanced resource density for memory-bound applications, functioning effectively for distributed in-memory caching layers, relational database engines, memory-resident ETL pipelines, and general business analytics workloads.
